exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal, cesarean with labor, cesarean without labor)
cohort: Singleton neonates born at less than 29 weeks' gestation
finding: Cesarean section was not associated with increased survival or decreased risk of neurodevelopmental impairment in premature singleton neonates born at less than 29 weeks' gestation.
mod_finding: The odds of composite outcome of mortality or neurodevelopmental impairment for neonates born via cesarean section without labor versus vaginal delivery, and cesarean section with labor versus vaginal delivery were 0.90 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.59 to 1.37) and 1.08 (95% CI: 0.72 to 1.61), respectively.
